attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed. Nobody else is being quoted.

semantics.note: The 'suggest that they want to try' hedge is kept in. The funding-decline part is a firm statement about the present, so 'observation' is the right kind. The intent part is hedged and is rightly left unscored.

contract.note: He named no measure, so the contract uses Q1 2023 against the 2021–early 2022 boom. That is a fair, ordinary reading. Treating the automation clause only as a noticeable lean toward AI, rather than all of the money, is fair and not stretched either way. Because the period and baseline were chosen by the evaluator, the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Crunchbase, Q1 2023: global funding was $76B, down 53% from $162B a year earlier. This is a large, clear drop against the baseline the contract requires.

CB Insights, Q1 2023: $58.6B, down 13% from the previous quarter after earlier quarterly drops, and back to pre-pandemic levels. It compares with the prior quarter, not the prior year, but it is consistent with a sustained decline from the boom.

Crunchbase: AI-tagged companies took 19% of Q1 2023 dollars and AI was called a bright spot while other sectors fell. That satisfies the AI-tilt secondary point, read as a lean rather than all of the money.
Record unspent fund money (about $580B) as of end-2022. This is a different measure and an earlier date, so it is background only, not evidence of the outcome.

reviews.rationale: Two trackers show Q1 2023 venture funding far below boom levels: Crunchbase reports a 53% fall from the year before, and CB Insights a continuing slide to pre-pandemic levels. AI was a favoured, growing area, at 19% of dollars. The unread Inc. article suggests AI may not have been the single largest category, but the contract does not require that. The intent behind the automation clause is hedged and not scored.
